main_body: multi-gable timber-framed building with tiled roof
top_band: red-brown and golden-yellow tiled roof slopes from row 0 to row 76 (main twin gables) and row 20 to row 63 (central connecting roof)
evidence: The building clearly shows foreshortened upper roof slopes (rows 0-76 on the twin gables, rows 20-63 on the central roof) sitting above the vertical timber-framed plaster walls (rows 61-143). Under the eaves and gables (e.g. rows 64-65, 80-81) there is a distinct dark eave shadow, and the windows and door are recessed within timber frames.

style.evidence: This piece is directly from the Beodeul chipset itself, using the exact same roof tile pattern (6-step ramp from pale yellow highlight to deep maroon-brown), speckled plaster texture, timber framing, and door/window details as the reference houses.
